criteria.evidence: Every required section is substantive: What it does ("Runs after the setup answers are confirmed. It records which rule groups of the review fit the project and which do not"), Inputs / Outputs ("It holds one entry per rule group: the group's name, kept or skipped, and the question and answer that decided it"), Rules & behavior (six answer-to-group mappings plus the default-keep and rerun rules), five Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, Out of scope naming /check-change, fn-setup-questions and the review's own memory, and an Agent intent (ICE) section with Goal, Limit, Fails if, Context and Checked by lines.

"A database group on a project with no database gives only noise, but a group skipped by mistake hides real findings, so only a clear answer can skip one."; "Database no: the database group is skipped, because there is no schema, query or data store for its rules to check."; "it is never skipped by another answer, because a leak of personal data is the costliest miss."; "kept in the product profile beside the setup answers, so the review reads it where every later play reads the project's facts."

Every section is discrete bullets; the feature states the function's behavior ("It records which rule groups of the review fit the project"), never a user story; acceptance is Given/When/Then: "Given answers that say there is no front end, no back-end service, no database and no running service, when the rule groups are chosen, then the record marks those four groups as skipped, each with the answer that decided it."

Parent capability gives one line: "Choose the review rule groups (fn-review-rule-groups): records which rule groups of the review fit the project, so a review runs only those and names the groups it skipped." The feature adds the record's shape and home ("one entry per rule group: the group's name, kept or skipped, and the question and answer that decided it"), the six answer-to-group mappings, the default-keep rule for unspoken groups, the Garura-specific permission-group handling and testable acceptance criteria.

What: "A rule group is a set of the review's rules that check one kind of thing ... the review runs or skips a group as a whole, so this feature decides per group, never per rule." Why: "That is how the product owner sees that a review did not run a rule and why." and the #860 source ("the review of PR #858 ran database, permission and front-end rules on Garura's own tool files"). Edges: "A group no answer speaks to is kept, so a rule is never skipped by silence."; Out of scope names the review play, Ask the setup questions and the review's own memory as owners.
